preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(line.split()[0]) <= 100000 and 1 <= int(line.split()[1]) <= 200000 for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: The first line contains integers n (1 ≤ n ≤ 100 000) and m (1 ≤ m ≤ 200 000), where n is the number of computers and m is the number of existing cables. Each subsequent line contains two integers ai and bi (1 ≤ ai, bi ≤ n) representing a cable between computers ai and bi.
The input consists of exactly m + 1 lines: the first line with n and m, followed by m lines of cable connections.

postconditions.expression: stdout.splitlines()[0].strip() == str(p) and p >= m and p <= 500000
postconditions.description: The first line of the output is an integer p (p ≥ m), representing the minimum number of cables in the final scheme, which does not exceed 500 000.

postconditions.expression: all(len(line.split()) == 2 and 1 <= int(line.split()[0]) <= n and 1 <= int(line.split()[1]) <= n for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:p+1])
postconditions.description: Each of the next p lines contains two integers ci and di (1 ≤ ci, di ≤ n), representing a directed cable from ci to di.

postconditions.expression: all((ai, bi) in [(c, d) for c, d in stdout.splitlines()[1:p+1]] or (bi, ai) in [(c, d) for c, d in stdout.splitlines()[1:p+1]] for ai, bi in [tuple(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]])
postconditions.description: All original cables (ai, bi) must appear in the output as either (ai, bi) or (bi, ai), meaning their direction is chosen.

postconditions.expression: all(len([d for c, d in stdout.splitlines()[1:p+1] if c == i]) % 2 == 0 for i in range(1, n + 1))
postconditions.description: For every computer i, the number of cables directed out of it (out-degree) must be even, ensuring all cables can be grouped into pairs.

postconditions.expression: all(len([d for c, d in stdout.splitlines()[1:p+1] if d == i]) % 2 == 0 for i in range(1, n + 1))
postconditions.description: For every computer i, the number of cables directed into it (in-degree) must be even, ensuring all cables can be grouped into pairs.

postconditions.expression: all(len([d for c, d in stdout.splitlines()[1:p+1] if c == i and d == j]) <= 1 for i in range(1, n + 1) for j in range(1, n + 1))
postconditions.description: No duplicate directed cables exist between the same pair of computers (i, j).
